question.text: An object moves along a straight path such that it maintains a constant speed v₁ for the initial half of its total travel duration, and a constant speed v₂ for the final half of the duration. Determine the average speed of the object throughout the entire trip.
conditions: speed during first half of total time is v₁
speed during second half of total time is v₂

figure.description: A line segment from point A to point B split at a point C into two sections: section AC corresponds to duration t, speed v₁, and distance d₁; section CB corresponds to duration t, speed v₂, and distance d₂.

solution.approach: When the two speeds each last for equal time, the average speed is the arithmetic mean, found from total distance over total time.

steps.text: Let each half of the total time be t, so the total time is 2t.
Find the distance covered in each half from distance = speed multiplied by time.
Average speed is total distance over total time.

common_mistakes.text: Using the harmonic mean 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂), which applies only when the two parts are equal in distance, not equal in time.
